name: LPmud 1.4.1-A
english_description: A historically significant early LPMud reference mudlib, bundled together with its own classic C-language LPMud driver source (ignored entirely here -- this project uses its own FluffOS build). Only the archive's mudlib/ directory (338 files) was ported: doc/{build,efun} reference docs, obj/ (arm/armor/door/guard/corpse/soul/wiz_soul/player etc.), room/ (the original 'HMC LP-mud' game world -- Endoplasmatorium, village green, clinic, elevator, mines, a maze), and players/. The bundled driver's version string and internal history (README/CHANGES files) place this squarely in the pre-'master object' era of LPMud (predating the security-daemon/uid architecture that TMI-2, Nightmare, Genesis and every later LPMud/MudOS/FluffOS descendant standardized on): the driver source has zero references to a master object anywhere, hardcodes clone_object("obj/player") + logon() for new connections, and hardcodes loading room/init_file's listed objects at boot. Porting this to a modern master-object-requiring driver needed a master.lpc and simul_efun.lpc authored from scratch (pure driver-glue: get_root_uid/get_bb_uid, permissive valid_read/valid_write matching the original's total absence of a mudlib-level ACL, a connect() reproducing the driver's own hardcoded clone-and-logon, and an epilog()/preload() pair reproducing its boot-time init_file loader) -- no mudlib content was invented. Beyond that, this driver's own closed set of built-in keywords/efuns diverges sharply from every later LPC dialect it inspired: add_action()+add_verb() is a two-call verb-registration idiom (~300 call sites, mechanically merged into single two-argument add_action() calls, since add_verb() doesn't exist at all on this driver and the verb argument is mandatory here); move_object(item, dest) moves an ARBITRARY object (not just the caller) at ~200 call sites, requiring both a call-site rewrite to the modern item->move_object(dest) idiom AND a universal move_object() LPC wrapper (this driver's call_other() never falls through to a real efun of the same name) plus a resolve_ob() helper restoring this archive's own find-object-or-load-it semantics that the real move_object() efun's string-destination handling doesn't provide; and reset(arg) with arg==0 meaning "first-ever setup" is expected to fire synchronously right after an object is created -- true on the original driver, but this driver defers an object's first reset() by a full `time to reset` interval (~15-30 minutes) after create(), so a universal create(){call_other(this_object(),"reset",0);} was added to the global include file to restore that behavior for every room/NPC/item archive-wide (confirmed via a from-scratch read of the driver's own object-lifecycle C++, not guesswork). Smaller fixes: the old `status` type keyword (->int), a bullboard command function illegally named `new` (a struct-class keyword on this driver) plus a same-function author typo (envorinment->environment), `class` used as a plain identifier in two rooms (now a struct-class keyword), 1-arg crypt()/snoop() calls upgraded to this driver's mandatory 2-arg forms, an archive-wide security.h (wizard-level/invisibility-level constants) that lived one directory above the mudlib/ root in the original tarball layout, and simul_efun shims for a half-dozen driver-only classic efuns (transfer, log_file, cat, ls, people, create_wizard -- all faithfully reimplemented from the driver's own C source; add_worth/wizlist/localcmd left as honest no-op stubs, since they exposed purely internal driver bookkeeping the mudlib never had access to). End to end verified: register a new character (with a plain 26-letter name -- the archive's own valid_name() predates non-ASCII support entirely), reach the starting room lit and fully described, move between rooms, `soul on` + emote commands, score, save, quit, and reconnect into the same saved character across a driver restart.
